text:
alex: Heads up — nightly infra perf regression for Mistral-family endpoints. p95 latency jumped ~3x on long-seq workloads after the kernel-router change last night. Digging in.
maria: ugh. which change exactly? the router that picks fp8-vs-fp16 kernels?
todd: yep the commit is linked in deploy: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/commit/8f7a3a — it adds a heuristic to prefer fp8 kernels for KV cache hits when mem pressure low.
alex: root cause looks like kernel selection misclassifies when RoPE phase wraps. For some Mistral sequences (~>4k tokens) the kernel router tries fp8-kv path but the head-dim alignment is slightly off, causing fallback into a slow generic path and an extra copy. p95 went from ~160ms -> ~520ms on Mixtral-8B.
jisoo: any perf profiler traces?
alex: yes — attached snippet from runtime profiler:
```
[runtime] route_decision: model=mistral-8b, seq=4200, kv_size=3.9GB, fav_fp8=true
[kernel] select: candidate=fp8_kv_pack_v2 -> validate_alignment FAILED (rotary_stride_mismatch)
[kernel] fallback: generic_attn_gemm (extra kv pack) + memcpy
latencies: select=1.2ms validate=4.6ms pack=38ms gemm=430ms memcpy=28ms
```
maria: rotary_stride_mismatch — that sounds like RoPE scaling interaction with kv packing layout. We saw weird wrap artifacts in encoder tests earlier.
todd: also saw increased tail memory churn: KV eviction rate spiked. Eviction log:
```
evict event: model=mistral-8b, total_kv=3.9GB, free_buf=120MB, policy=LRU_PREFETCH
evicted_keys=12, evict_latency=18ms, quant_drop=fp8->fp16 adjust
```
alex: hypothesis: fp8 quantized KV + current eviction heuristics + RoPE wrap leads to misaligned strides so kernel validation rejects and falls back to slow path. On top of that, the fallback path doesn't use the prefetched prefix cache so we do extra reads.
jisoo: can we reproduce locally with a synthetic workload? I can run a deterministic seq that causes rotational stride to wrap.
alex: pls do. test command I used:
```
runtime-driver --model mistral-8b --seq-len 4200 --batch 1 --prefetch=on --kv-precision=auto --dump-kv-layout /tmp/kv.dump
```
jisoo: running now.
infra-bot: deploy 1806123400 -> prod-rt finished with status FAILED. See logs: /ci/1806123400/rt-deploy.log
maria: decision options: (A) rollback kernel-router commit (fast), (B) tighten validation to prefer fp16 when phase-wrap detected, (C) disable fp8-kv for Mistral families and leave router on. Thoughts?
todd: for short-term, C seems safest — disable fp8-kv for mistral/mixtral until we fix alignment. Rolling kernel-router back will lose other perf wins.
alex: agreed. also add a profiling hook to log rotary-phase mod stride for each route decision so we have telemetry.
jisoo: reproducer done. confirms mismatch at seq 4096 boundary. I pushed a small test harness: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/pull/2145
maria: ok I'll open a hotfix PR to gate fp8-kv by model+rotary-check and add the telemetry. assign to todd for review.
alex: can we also change batching heuristic to prefer smaller batches when KV saturation >85%? Large batches magnify the fallback cost.
todd: yes — batch-shaper flag `--batch-shape-threshold=0.85` in runtime config. I'll stage on canary.
alex: action items:
 - maria: PR to disable fp8-kv for mistral families + add rotary-phase telemetry (PR #2146) (due today)
 - todd: canary batch-shaper tweak + deploy rollback plan if canary spikes (due now)
 - jisoo: consolidate reproducer and test vectors in /qa/kv-rope-wrap (done)
 - alex: followup to add unit test for kernel validation to accept aligned fp8 layouts only when stride % head_dim == 0
maria: ping me once canary is up, I'll ship the hotfix.
todd: starting canary now.
infra-bot: canary deploy 1806123470 -> prod-rt-canary started
alex: thanks — we'll regroup in 30m. :coffee:
